\begin{abstract}
Accessibility Fix (benchmark-accessibility-fix) is a public npm benchmark package in the benchmark-* family, version 0.1.0, status alpha. This report records what the package measures in its own words, its deterministic grader and its SDK, CLI, MCP and HTTP surfaces, and the offline validation the family data holds: a scripted good policy mean of 1 and a scripted bad policy mean of 0 over 40 tasks, from mock runs at seeds 1 and 2 on the public task split generated with seed 20261015. The review record shows 3 fix rounds, 2 defect classes with public locators, and 5 merged feature pull requests of which 3 were approved. It was not part of the preregistered trivial-policy check. No real-model scores are reported. Software concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23422402, family paper DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23428802.
\end{abstract}
\section{What the package asks}
The package states its question in its own README:
% quote: benchmark-accessibility-fix/README.md#L7
\begin{quote}
benchmark-accessibility-fix measures whether a model can repair a
broken web page so keyboard, screen-reader, and contrast checks pass
\textemdash{} and whether the repair is genuine rather than deleted or
hidden content.
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-accessibility-fix/blob/v0.1.0/README.md#L7}{\texttt{benchmark-accessibility-fix:README.md\#L7}}.}

Its index entry states the measured construct as: ``Whether a fixed HTML page really repairs injected keyboard, screen-reader, and contrast defects without deleting or hiding content.'' (\texttt{paper/data/suite.json}, \texttt{benchmark-accessibility-fix.whatItMeasures}).

\section{Grader and surfaces}
The grading document states the mechanism in its own words:
% quote: benchmark-accessibility-fix/docs/grading.md#L3
\begin{quote}
This file is written BEFORE the grader code. It lists how the
deterministic grader can fail or be gamed, and what it does about each
case. The analyzer itself lives in \texttt{src/a11y.ts} and stays
dependency-free: a light HTML parser plus a small CSS cascade
(specificity, source order, inheritance), no browser and no runtime
layout engine.
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-accessibility-fix/blob/v0.1.0/docs/grading.md#L3}{\texttt{benchmark-accessibility-fix:docs/grading.md\#L3}}.}

The index entry summarises the grader as: ``Deterministic static analysis of the fixed HTML: ten WCAG-cited checks score defects fixed, minus regressions, content loss, element removal, and hiding abuse. Model judging is off.'' (\texttt{paper/data/suite.json}, \texttt{benchmark-accessibility-fix.grader}).

\section{Offline validation}
No real model was run. The family data records mock runs at seeds \pkgMockSeedA{} and \pkgMockSeedB{}
over the public task split generated with seed \pkgPublicSeed{}, on version \pkgVersion{}:
the scripted good policy reaches a mean of \pkgGoodMean{} (weakest task \pkgGoodMin{}),
the scripted bad policy a mean of \pkgBadMean{} (best task \pkgBadMax{}),
and the run at mock seed \pkgMockSeedA{} scores \pkgMockMean{} over \pkgTaskCount{} tasks
with a bootstrap interval of \pkgMockCiLow{} to \pkgMockCiHigh{} (\pkgMockPassed{} tasks passed; cost \$\pkgMockCost{}).
Source: \texttt{paper/data/suite.json}, collected by \texttt{scripts/collect.mjs}.

\section{Preregistered trivial-policy check}
The check design is described in the family paper: trivial policies ran each package in the registered set
at \pkgTrivialVerOld{} and \pkgTrivialVerNew{} through a local fake model server answering through
the package's own OpenAI provider (\texttt{paper/sections/prereg.tex}).
This package was not part of the preregistered check, so \texttt{paper/data/trivial.csv} carries no row for it.
\section{Limitations and what is not claimed}
The package documents its own limit:
% quote: benchmark-accessibility-fix/README.md#L222
\begin{quote}
The static analyzer cannot run layout, zoom, or assistive technology.
Contrast resolves hex, \texttt{rgb()}, \texttt{hsl()}, the full
named-color list, \texttt{var()} custom properties, and
\texttt{inherit} through a small cascade. Concealment that leaves the
element in the parsed render \textemdash{} \texttt{clip-path},
\texttt{transform: scale(0)}, zero height, \texttt{font-size: 1px},
off-screen positioning \textemdash{} is neither rewarded nor penalized
today (the same machinery powers the legitimate \texttt{.sr-only}
pattern); the E2E gate pins that policy. Hard tasks share one
generator family, so a fixer written against it would clear the tier;
the benchmark claims difficulty against unseen structure, not
template-proofness. Fixtures are small synthetic pages, not production
sites. Public tasks can enter training data, so keep a separately
seeded hidden split for final comparisons. Remote providers can add
cost and retain prompts under their own policies.
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-accessibility-fix/blob/v0.1.0/README.md#L222}{\texttt{benchmark-accessibility-fix:README.md\#L222}}.}

This report claims no model capability: it records no real-model run, no leaderboard, and no comparison between models.
These offline numbers describe the graders and the scripted policies. They say nothing about a hosted model.
Package status is \texttt{\pkgStatus{}}; saturation is \texttt{\pkgSaturation{}} (\texttt{paper/data/suite.json}).
Disclosure: the package was built by AI coding agents in sessions the author configured, the reviews cited here
are agent reviews, and this report was generated by \texttt{scripts/pkg-reports.mjs} on \pkgSnapshotDate{} from the cached sources named above.
